title: Two Indian-Origin Men Jailed for Total of 28 Years Over Leeds Racing Crash That Killed Mother and Daughter
excerpt: Jasskamal Riyat was jailed for 16 years and Hardeep Bhachu for 12 years at Leeds Crown Court for causing the deaths of Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her four-year-old daughter Lena Czepczor on Scott Hall Road in January 2023.
body:
• Jasskamal Riyat, 37, was sentenced to 16 years and Hardeep Bhachu, 29, to 12 years at Leeds Crown Court on Monday — 28 years in total — for causing death by dangerous driving.
  • Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her daughter Lena Czepczor, four, were walking to school on Scott Hall Road on 16 January 2023 when Bhachu lost control of his Audi TT RS and hit them; both died at the scene.
  • Bhachu pleaded guilty in June 2024; Riyat, who was racing him in a BMW and left the scene, denied involvement and was convicted by a jury in August.
  • Both men received six-year driving bans and must take an extended driving test before driving again.

Two Indian-origin men have been jailed for a total of 28 years after their racing on a Leeds dual carriageway killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they walked to school. Hardeep Bhachu, 29, of Grant Row, Adel, pleaded guilty at Leeds Crown Court in June 2024 to causing the deaths of Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her daughter Lena Czepczor by dangerous driving, and was sentenced on Monday to 12 years, according to West Yorkshire Police.

Jasskamal Riyat, 37, of Buckstone Avenue, Moortown, was found guilty by a jury in August of two counts of causing death by dangerous driving and was sentenced at the same hearing to 16 years. CCTV and dashcam footage showed he had been racing Bhachu immediately before the collision.

"A road is not a race track. A powerful car is not an invitation to test its limits on a public road."

— Judge Ray Singh, sentencing at Leeds Crown Court

What happened on Scott Hall Road

Shortly after 8:30 a.m. on 16 January 2023, Bhachu lost control of the Audi TT RS he was driving and hit Justyna and Lena before colliding with the wall of the Vertu Jaguar Leeds dealership on Scott Hall Road. The mother and daughter, who had been walking to school, both died at the scene. The two men did not know each other; minutes earlier they had spoken through their car windows at a traffic light, congratulating each other on the power of their cars, the court heard, according to Indian White Paper.

https://x.com/CrimeLdn/status/2114736482007072983

Riyat witnessed the collision but left the scene instead of stopping. He denied his involvement and was convicted on the extensive dashcam and CCTV footage showing his speeding vehicle in the moments before the crash.

"An innocent mother and daughter who were simply making their way to school never made it there and tragically never made it home because of the selfish, reckless actions of these two men."

— Detective Inspector Paul Conroy, West Yorkshire Police

The end of a long process

Detective Inspector Paul Conroy, of the Major Collision Enquiry Team, said the sentencing marked the end of a long criminal justice process for the family, noting it was over two years since Bhachu admitted his part and that the wait for justice had taken its toll, according to Hello Rayo. Police released video of the moments leading up to the collision, saying they hoped it would make people think about their own driving.

Both men were given six-year driving bans and will have to take an extended driving test. No sentence, police acknowledged, will compensate the family for two lives lost on a school walk — but the court's message, in Judge Singh's words, was that the consequences of competitive driving at extreme speed were, in this case, irreversible.
